text: SABECO brings communities and generations together at Ok Om Bok Festival 2026

HÀ NỘI - Saigon Beer-Alcohol-Beverage Corporation (SABECO), a Vietnamese brewer with more than 150 years of history, is joining the Ok Om Bok Festival 2026 in Cần Thơ City and Vĩnh Long Province from November 18 to 24, seeking to promote the cultural heritage of the Mekong Delta and strengthen community ties.

The participation comes as Việt Nam prepares to celebrate its first Việt Nam Culture Day on November 24, highlighting the role of traditional festivals in bringing people together and fostering pride in the country's cultural diversity.
Việt Nam's cultural festivals offer opportunities for people from different regions to meet, share experiences and celebrate their common heritage.
The Ok Om Bok Festival, celebrated by the Khmer community in southern Việt Nam, is one such occasion.
Rooted in the tradition of giving thanks to the Moon deity and praying for favourable harvests and prosperity, the festival has been recognised as a national intangible cultural heritage.
It also provides a platform for communities to gather, strengthen bonds and pass down cultural traditions through generations.
Today, the festival attracts visitors from across the country, helping showcase the distinctive culture of the Mekong Delta while promoting cultural exchange and local tourism.
As the culture of the southwestern region is an integral part of Việt Nam's national identity, the celebration and promotion of Ok Om Bok also serve to strengthen the country's shared cultural pride.
A Vietnamese business connecting communities
With more than 150 years of history in Việt Nam, SABECO places strong emphasis on community engagement and the preservation of the country's cultural heritage.

The company seeks to promote and connect cultural celebrations that reflect Vietnamese identity, creating opportunities for people of different generations and regions to share experiences and take pride in their common values.
This commitment is particularly evident in the Mekong Delta, where SABECO has maintained a long-standing presence through four breweries and two trading companies.

Alongside its business operations, SABECO and its subsidiaries have carried out various community programmes, including installing solar-powered streetlights in rural areas, upgrading community sports facilities and providing support during the annual Tết (Lunar New Year) celebrations.
Through years of engagement, the company has gained a deeper understanding of local cultural life and the values cherished by communities in the region.
This year, as part of its nationwide activities marking Việt Nam Culture Day, SABECO is bringing that spirit of connection to the Ok Om Bok Festival.
Working with Cần Thơ City and Vĩnh Long Province, the company aims to provide more opportunities for residents and visitors to explore and experience traditional cultural values.
Patsy Lim, SABECO's deputy general director in charge of marketing, said the festival's significance extended beyond the excitement of its signature boat races.
"What makes Ok Om Bok so meaningful is not only the excitement of the Ngo boat race, but the spirit of togetherness it represents.
Every crew carries the pride of its own hometown, yet the celebration brings people from different communities and generations together in a shared sense of joy and belonging," she said.
"As a proud Vietnamese brewer, SABECO believes that the unique cultural traditions of every region are an important part of what connects us as a nation.

Through Bia Saigon, we are proud to celebrate the rich heritage of the Mekong Delta and create more opportunities for people to come together, share in that pride and experience the spirit of Ok Om Bok.

"More importantly, we hope these shared experiences will inspire younger generations to develop their own connection with these traditions, so that the cultural pride and spirit of togetherness they represent continue to be celebrated for years to come.

The festival is taking place in Vĩnh Long from November 18 to 24 and in Cần Thơ from November 21 to 24. Alongside traditional ceremonies, the programme features cultural performances, music, food and community activities.
One of the highlights will be the Ngo boat races on November 23 and 24 on the Maspéro River, which runs through Sóc Trăng and Phú Lợi wards in Cần Thơ City.
The traditional sporting event is closely associated with the cultural life of local communities.
Each boat brings together a team of rowers who must work in perfect coordination, relying on endurance, teamwork and a shared sense of purpose.
The excitement of the competition, combined with the enthusiastic cheers of spectators lining both banks of the river, has become a defining feature of the festival.
Inspired by this spirit, SABECO and its Bia Saigon brand will introduce a series of activities under the theme "The Resounding Beat of the Drum" at this year's festival.
During each race, the rhythmic beat of the drum sets the pace for the rowers, reflecting their unity and the collective enthusiasm of spectators along the riverbanks.
It also symbolises the shared heartbeat of a united community.
As Việt Nam celebrates its first Culture Day on November 24, SABECO's participation in Ok Om Bok carries particular significance.

The activities aim to ensure that the cultural heritage of the Mekong Delta continues to be valued, preserved and shared with a wider audience, as an integral part of Việt Nam's rich and diverse national identity. -VNS
